instruction_summary: Produce a calibrated 2026 theory update for Shimer (2012): recalibrate the flow model's central parameters, add the smallest amendment (a rare state-dependent layoff regime) that reconciles the finding-driven original with the 2020 separation shock and the secular flow decline, and validate it out-of-sample.

steps.description: Rebuilt venv; read paper model section (eqs 4-5, Table 1 decomposition), replication report, and 001 artifacts
steps.command: uv venv && uv pip install numpy scipy pandas statsmodels matplotlib requests; pdftotext paper.pdf

steps.description: Recalibrate era parameters (F,X,omega,rho,half-life,u*,steady-state corr); regime-conditional decomposition (broad + extreme layoff regime); monthly per-recession finding-vs-separation episode decomposition; OOS classifier pre-2015 -> 2015-2026
Assemble paper-era-vs-2026 calibration_table.csv and the 2-panel flagship figure (mechanism original-vs-updated; secular slowdown + rising persistence)
Wrote theory_update.md (publication-quality theory section, all claims labelled ESTIMATED/CALIBRATED/PROPOSED), report.md, result_card.json

key_results.oos_classifier: pre-2015-trained rule flags EXACTLY Mar-Apr 2020 in 2015-2026, no false positives

comparison_to_original.note: Shimer's flagged secular decline in X continued through 2026; recalibrated here.
Cannot coexist with normal-regime 0.89 under a constant beta -> motivates the regime amendment.
Regime anchor: separations dominate only across 2020.
Approximation degrades as adjustment speed omega falls; breaks in fast 2020 shock.
New forward-looking implication: lower but stickier natural rate.

deviations: No likelihood-based Markov-switching estimation (compute-modest instruction): pi_L is a frequency and regime beta's are the paper's OLS decomposition on regime subsamples / 001's windows -- calibration to moments 001 already produced, stated plainly.

beta_F^L magnitude is calibrated to the 2020-inclusive windows, not predicted out-of-sample: 2020 is the only extreme layoff episode on record, so a pre-2015 mixture under-predicts the 2015-2026 flip -- reported honestly as the tail-risk finding, not hidden.

2020 is a sub-quarterly event; analysis is deliberately monthly and the clipped March-2020 F-point is handled with a clip-immune separation hypothetical (per the known clip artifact; with the clip kept, recent steady-state corr spuriously collapses to 0.24).
Levels of F_bar/X_bar carry the duration-misreporting caveat inherited from 001; ratio-based omega/rho/u* are more robust than the levels.
Demographic heterogeneity (paper C4/Figure 3) untouched -- needs CPS microdata, out of scope as in 001.
